description: Mutable default argument causes shared state
buggy_code:
def add_item(item, items=[]):
    items.append(item)
    return items

list1 = add_item("apple")
print(list1)  # ['apple'] — correct

list2 = add_item("banana")
print(list2)  # Expected: ['banana'], Got: ['apple', 'banana']
traceback:
No exception raised.
Expected: add_item("banana") returns ['banana']
Actual: add_item("banana") returns ['apple', 'banana']
The default list is shared between calls.

ground_truth.root_cause: Mutable default argument items=[] is created once at function definition time and shared across all calls — should use None as default and create new list inside function
